open_points.subject: A04 check order for pointer withdrawals
open_points.text: “(2) for agent authority, the session and its set ...; (3) that every record the action names exists” conflicts with A08: “A withdrawal names the pointer only; its project is the pointer's own, and for Kernel that project is checked against the session's set.”
open_points.question: How can Registry perform the stage-2 project-set check for a pointer-only withdrawal before stage 3 establishes that the pointer exists and reveals its project?
options: Look up the pointer provisionally during stage 2 solely to perform the hidden authorization check
Check pointer existence first but collapse absent and outside-set outcomes into the same not-found answer
Require the withdrawal request to name the project as well as the pointer
open_points.default_guess: Look up the pointer provisionally without exposing whether it exists, then return the same not-found answer for absence or an outside-set project.

open_points.subject: A04 placement of malformed identities and versions
open_points.text: “(3) that every record the action names exists ...; (4) the values given ...; (5) the stated revision or access version” does not say where an identity, revision or access version that cannot be parsed is checked.
open_points.question: Does a malformed record identity fail as nonexistence at stage 3 or as an invalid value at stage 4, and does a missing or malformed revision/version fail at stage 4 or stage 5?
options: Treat malformed identities and malformed revisions or versions as stage-4 value failures
Treat malformed identities as stage-3 not-found and revisions or versions as stage-5 failures
Define separate placement for missing, malformed and stale values
open_points.default_guess: Treat syntactically malformed values as stage 4, then perform existence at stage 3 only after successful identifier parsing internally while preserving the declared outward precedence.

open_points.subject: A13 owner-session cookie
open_points.text: “carried by a cookie that scripts cannot read, sent only over HTTPS when the interface is reached from another machine, and only to Registry's own origin”
open_points.question: What exact cookie scope and browser attributes enforce this rule, especially since cookies are scoped by domain and path rather than by origin and are not isolated by port?
options: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, host-only, Path=/
HttpOnly and host-only, with Secure only on externally reached HTTPS and a narrower owner-interface path
Another explicit set of Domain, Path, SameSite, Secure and persistence attributes
open_points.default_guess: Use an HttpOnly, host-only, SameSite=Strict cookie with Path=/ and Secure whenever Registry is served over HTTPS; keep all server-side lifetime checks authoritative.

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent sign-out and admitted session-changing request
open_points.text: “a request that passes it completes even if ... a sign-out comes while it runs” and “requests ... that change its state ... are applied ... in the order in which they take the session's one lock, after passing the session check”
open_points.question: If request A passes the session check, request B signs out and takes the session lock first, and A takes the lock afterward, does A still change the store or session, or is it stopped because B ended the session?
options: Admission before sign-out guarantees that A completes even if it acquires the lock later
Lock order governs, so B ending the session prevents A's later change
Store changes admitted before sign-out complete, but session-local changes such as an upload are discarded
open_points.default_guess: Admission guarantees completion of A's atomic store action, but A must not recreate or retain session-local state after sign-out.

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation-input binding
open_points.text: “kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order” and “a submission's inputs are bound when their digest equals it”
open_points.question: What exact serialization, field order, normalization and digest algorithm define equality of confirmation inputs, including absent versus blank values and collections such as import picks?
options: Digest a canonical State-6 representation with sorted or schema-fixed fields
Digest the raw submitted form bytes
Store structured normalized inputs and compare them directly instead of relying only on a digest
open_points.default_guess: Digest a versioned canonical serialization using schema order, A02 normalization and a specified cryptographic hash.

open_points.subject: A16 migration file identity
open_points.text: “The mapping names the file by its digest” and “closure.file_digest = digest(f)”
open_points.question: Which digest algorithm is used, and is it computed over the exact uploaded bytes, decoded records, or a canonical serialization of the file?
options: A specified cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes
A digest of the parsed canonical migration document
Both a raw-file digest and a canonical-content digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a specified cryptographic digest of the exact uploaded bytes so the confirmed file is unambiguous.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only configuration
open_points.text: Rule 1 allows “for an owner-only start, none of the four” service tokens, while rule 2 checks “every item of rule 1 present.”
open_points.question: During an owner-only start, are the four service-token items exempt from the presence check, and do blank token variables count as absent or malformed?
options: All four variables must be absent; their presence with blank values is malformed
All four may be absent or blank
Owner-only mode requires a separate explicit configuration item
open_points.default_guess: Exempt the four token items only when all four variables are absent; any present blank or partial set fails.

open_points.subject: A17 environment-variable contract
open_points.text: “the set of environment variables whose names begin with REGISTRY_” and “each well formed”
open_points.question: What are the exact variable names and accepted encodings or syntax for the store path, backup path, backup key, owner credential and four tokens?
options: Specify one exact variable name and textual encoding for each item
Derive names mechanically from the item and service names
Leave names and formats to each release
open_points.default_guess: Specify stable exact names; interpret paths as filesystem paths and secrets as an explicitly encoded byte sequence.

open_points.subject: A17 secret length
open_points.text: “A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long” although the secrets come from environment variables.
open_points.question: Under which encoding is an environment string converted to bytes for the 32-byte length, equality and constant-time comparison checks?
options: UTF-8 bytes of the environment value
A required base64 decoding to raw bytes
A required hexadecimal decoding to raw bytes
open_points.default_guess: Require a documented base64 encoding and perform all checks on the decoded bytes.

open_points.subject: A17 first failed startup check
open_points.text: “every item of rule 1 present and none unknown” and “Within one check, items go in the order rule 1 lists them.”
open_points.question: If configuration has both a missing required item and an unknown REGISTRY_ item, which diagnostic wins, and in what order are unknown items considered when several exist?
options: Check listed missing items first, then unknown names in lexical order
Reject unknown names before checking missing items
Report all failures in the first check rather than only one
open_points.default_guess: Check required listed items in their declared order, then unknown names in Unicode lexical order.

open_points.subject: A17 startup cleanup
open_points.text: “A failed start leaves no file it made but a probe it could not remove, which the next start or run removes with the other temporary files.”
open_points.question: What startup step removes a probe or temporary file left by an earlier failed start, and does failure to remove it stop the new start?
options: Cleanup is a startup check and any failure stops startup
Startup makes a distinct new probe and leaves old cleanup to the next backup run
Cleanup is best-effort and startup continues after a diagnostic
open_points.default_guess: Make cleanup an explicit startup check before probing; failure stops startup without serving.

open_points.subject: A18 backup cryptography and authenticated metadata
open_points.text: “Each backup is encrypted with the backup key” and it records metadata “readable without its key,” but no encryption, authentication, key derivation or metadata-integrity rule is stated.
open_points.question: What cryptographic format protects the backup, and are the plaintext instant, release, sequence number and key digest authenticated against tampering?
options: A specified authenticated-encryption format with the plaintext header as authenticated associated data
Encryption plus a separate authenticated header
Encryption without authenticated metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned authenticated-encryption format and authenticate every plaintext metadata field as associated data.

open_points.subject: A18 backup filenames and collision behavior
open_points.text: “Kept and temporary names begin with two different prefixes the release declares” and a passing backup “is renamed to its kept name.”
open_points.question: What are the exact prefixes and filename construction, and what happens if the kept target name already exists?
options: Timestamp plus unique random suffix; an existing target is a failure and is never overwritten
Timestamp alone; atomically replace an existing target
Monotonic run identifier stored outside the backups
open_points.default_guess: Use fixed documented prefixes and a UTC timestamp plus random suffix; never overwrite an existing kept backup.

open_points.subject: A18 retention cleanup after individual failures
open_points.text: “it deletes every kept backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before, and every file under the kept prefix that cannot be read as a backup” and “A step that fails ... writes a diagnostic.”
open_points.question: In what order are kept files examined, and if reading or deleting one file fails, does cleanup stop or continue with the remaining files?
options: Process names in a declared order and stop on the first failure
Process all files independently, report each failure, and delete everything else eligible
Attempt old valid backups first and unreadable files second
open_points.default_guess: Process filenames in lexical order, continue independently after per-file failures, and report every failure without deleting files whose eligibility cannot be established safely.

open_points.subject: A18 meaning of unreadable kept backup
open_points.text: “every file under the kept prefix that cannot be read as a backup”
open_points.question: Does “cannot be read as a backup” mean an invalid plaintext header, failed authentication or decryption with the current key, an unsupported older release format, or any failed integrity check?
options: Only a structurally invalid or unauthenticated backup is deleted
Anything the current release cannot fully decrypt and open is deleted
Older formats and unknown-key backups are retained, while malformed current-format files are deleted
open_points.default_guess: Delete only files conclusively malformed under their declared format; retain an otherwise valid older or differently keyed backup.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-key rotation
open_points.text: “older backups stay encrypted with the key they were made with, which the digest each backup records names”
open_points.question: Where is the obligation to retain each old key until its last backup expires, or what alternative keeps those backups restorable after rotation?
options: The owner must retain old keys, identified by digest, until no kept backup uses them
Registry re-encrypts retained backups under the new key
Backups under old keys may remain retained but intentionally unrestorable
open_points.default_guess: Require the owner to retain old keys securely until every backup using them has expired or been deleted.

open_points.subject: A18 one-day recovery bound
open_points.text: “while the daily runs succeed ... a restore loses at most a day of changes,” while “a 03:00 that finds a run still going makes no run of its own.”
open_points.question: Does a run that lasts beyond the next 03:00 count as succeeding for the one-day recovery bound, and what bounds the age of the snapshot it eventually keeps?
options: The bound requires every successful run to finish before the next scheduled run
The snapshot instant is taken at run completion, so a long successful run may still satisfy it
A long run that causes a skipped schedule explicitly lengthens the recovery point like a missed run
open_points.default_guess: Treat any run that causes a later scheduled run to be skipped as a missed run for the recovery bound, and measure recoverability from the snapshot instant.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession pending confirmation representation
open_points.text: M11 says the pending confirmation carries “the action, its target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to,” while A13 says the import inputs are “kept as a digest of those values ... never as the values themselves.”
open_points.question: Does the OwnerSession store the bound target, version and inputs themselves, or only one or more digests of them?
options: Store only a canonical digest plus the one-time value and shown instant
Store action, target and version directly but store sensitive inputs only as a digest
Store all structured bound values directly
open_points.default_guess: Store action, target and version directly and only a canonical digest of the potentially sensitive inputs.

open_points.subject: OwnerSession uploaded file after another session imports
open_points.text: M11 says an uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted,” while A16 says “a file another session keeps stays until that session ends.”
open_points.question: When one owner session successfully imports, are uploaded files held by all other sessions dropped immediately, or do they remain until replacement or session end?
options: Drop every session's uploaded import file when the closure is committed
Drop only the confirming session's file; other files remain but cannot be imported
Drop other sessions' files when they next make a request
open_points.default_guess: Drop only the confirming session's file and leave other session files until replacement or session end, with every confirmation refused by the closure.

open_points.subject: Starting from an encrypted backup after store loss
open_points.text: R0-89 says “the owner puts a backup in its place on the host ... and Registry starts on it as on any store,” while A17 requires the configured store file to open as a store and A18 says a backup is encrypted and must be decrypted into a separate temporary store file for checking.
open_points.question: Does Registry accept an encrypted backup container as its configured store, or must the owner first materialize a normal decrypted store file outside Registry?
options: The owner decrypts and materializes a store before Registry starts
Registry recognizes and restores an encrypted backup placed at the store path
A release-specific external recovery tool converts the backup to a store
open_points.default_guess: The owner or an external release tool must materialize a normal store file before startup; Registry never opens the encrypted backup container as its store.
